subject: Re: Commercial structure — flexible-rate orchestration + spot-reserve terms
messages:
From: procurement@apexlabs.com
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-12T09:17:00-08:00
Subject: RFP question — reserve vs burst pricing

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the product overview. As we refine our RFP commercial appendix, procurement has two follow-ups on pricing mechanics:

1) We expect a committed-reserve for baseline traffic (monthly token commit). Can you provide a simple mapping of commit -> effective rate per 1k prompt+completion tokens at 3 commit bands (100M, 500M, 2B)?

2) We want a graceful overage model. Our engineering team would like an automatic smoothing mechanism that avoids big month-to-month spikes. Do you offer a blended smoothing or spot-reserve construct that mixes discounted spot capacity with reserved capacity?

3) Finally, contractually we need an example invoice and a sample SOW appendix that shows how bursts are billed when spot capacity is used.

Can you respond with a concise commercial proposal and any sample invoice attachments? Timeline: we'd like a response by 2026-11-18.

Thanks,
Sarah Kim
Procurement Lead — Apex Labs
procurement@apexlabs.com

(Attachment: Apex-RFP-commercial-questions.pdf)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: procurement@apexlabs.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-13T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP question — reserve vs burst pricing

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear asks. High level answers below; I attached a short pricing appendix and an example invoice mock. Happy to walk through in a 30-min call if helpful.

Summary commercial construct (short):
- Baseline commit (monthly token commitment) priced in three bands (reference net effective $/1k tokens):
  * 100M/month -> $0.95 / 1k tokens
  * 500M/month -> $0.68 / 1k tokens
  * 2B/month -> $0.45 / 1k tokens
- Spot-reserve orchestration: your baseline consumption is served from reserved pools. When demand spikes, requests are first routed to available spot capacity (discounted rate) and then overflow to burst reserved capacity if spot is exhausted.
- Smoothing credit: if month N usage exceeds commit by X tokens, we apply a rolling 3-month smoothing window where 50% of the overage can be absorbed as a billable credit (applied to the following invoice) provided average usage over the 3-month window stays within 110% of commit. This prevents single-month invoice shocks.
- Overage rate logic: Spot rate = 30% discount to committed band rate; Burst reserved rate = 10% premium to committed band rate when functioning as guaranteed overflow.

Attached: redwood-pricing-appendix-v1.pdf (worksheets with band math) and example-invoice-apex.xlsx (line-item example).

Next steps: if this model looks acceptable I'll loop in Finance to produce an appendix with exact SKU names and SOW language for the draft contract.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
(Attachment: redwood-pricing-appendix-v1.pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, procurement@apexlabs.com
Date: 2026-11-15T13:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP question — reserve vs burst pricing

Sarah / team — quick add from pricing ops and legal perspective:

1) Tier fences: the band rates above are volume-anchored and measured on monthly consumed tokens. We will include a pro-rata day-of-month calculation for mid-month scale-ups.

2) True-up & credits: the smoothing credit is conditional on maintaining average usage within the 3-month tolerance; we will document computation examples in the appendix. Credits are applied as invoice line-item adjustments (negative line) rather than one-off cash refunds.

3) SLA/latency: when requests are routed to spot capacity, they carry the same API interface but reduced execution priority; latency SLOs for spot will be listed separately. If you require guaranteed latency for overflow peaks, we recommend the burst-reserved SKU.

4) Example concession: for APX pilot we can offer an introductory 12% upfront discount on the 100M band for the first 3 months (subject to signature by 2026-12-15).

I'll prepare the appendix language and a worked example invoice. Attaching the current draft appendix (internal).

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Sales Ops — Redwood Inference
(Attachment: internal-pricing-draft.pdf)

From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@apexlabs.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@apexlabs.com, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-18T08:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP question — reserve vs burst pricing

Aditya / Karthik — thanks, this is helpful. A couple of clarifications before we move to legal review: 

• Can you provide one worked example invoice for a month where: committed = 500M; usage = 750M; spot capacity used = 200M; burst reserved used = 50M? Show line items and how smoothing credit is applied.
• For the smoothing window, can you confirm the exact algorithm for the 50% absorption and whether credits can carry beyond 3 months if there is a continued overage?

If you can return that by EOD 2026-11-20 we can include it in the commercial appendix and loop in our contracting team.

Best,
Sarah

(Attachment requested: example-invoice and smoothing-math.xlsx)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: sarah.kim@apexlabs.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-22T16:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP question — reserve vs burst pricing (Worked invoice + algorithm)

Sarah — attached is the worked invoice and a short note on the smoothing algorithm. Key points: 

Worked invoice (example-invoice-apex.xlsx):
- Commit line: 500,000,000 tokens @ $0.68 /1k = $340,000 (baseline)
- Spot usage: 200,000,000 tokens @ spot rate ($0.68 * 0.70 /1k) = $95,200 (30% discount)
- Burst-reserved usage: 50,000,000 tokens @ burst rate ($0.68 * 1.10 /1k) = $37,400
- Gross for month = $472,600
- Smoothing credit calculation: overage = usage - commit = 250,000,000 tokens. Under 3-month smoothing rule, 50% of overage = 125,000,000 tokens are eligible to be credited. Credit value = eligible tokens * committed band rate /1k = 125,000,000/1k * $0.68 = $85,000 (applied as invoice credit line).
- Net invoice = $472,600 - $85,000 = $387,600

Smoothing algorithm notes (appendix):
- Compute month-by-month overage (O_t). For month T where O_t > 0, eligible credit = 0.5 * O_t, provided that average usage across months T..T+2 <= 1.10 * commit. If average usage exceeds 110% across the window, eligibility for that month is reduced proportionally. Credits are limited to a 3-month carry-forward; they cannot be applied beyond month T+2.

We also attached the pricing appendix with band math and the example-invoice. If this aligns, next step is to issue a commercial appendix draft for legal with the pilot concession applied.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
(Attachments: example-invoice-apex.xlsx, redwood-pricing-appendix-v1.pdf)
